Key Verses

Matthew 11:28-30 (KJV)

KJV

Come unto me, all ye that labour and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest. Take my yoke upon you, and learn of me; for I am meek and lowly in heart: and ye shall find rest unto your souls. For my yoke is easy, and my burden is light.

In simpler words

Come to me, all you who are troubled and weighted down with care, and I will give you rest.

What was going on

In this passage of Scripture, the focus is this: Come unto Me — spoken by Jesus to The weary and heavy laden.

What it means

Jesus invites anyone who is tired and weighed down to come to Him and find rest.

Heavy laden is the entry requirement—not having it together first.

Psalm 55:22 (KJV)

KJV

Cast thy burden upon the LORD, and he shall sustain thee: he shall never suffer the righteous to be moved.

What was going on

David under Saul’s pursuit and Doeg’s betrayal; cries from caves and defeat; God still rules.

What it means

Cast your cares on the Lord and He will sustain you.

Cast means transfer, not organize better.

Philippians 4:6-7 (KJV)

KJV

Be careful for nothing; but in every thing by prayer and supplication with thanksgiving let your requests be made known unto God. And the peace of God, which passeth all understanding, shall keep your hearts and minds through Christ Jesus.

In simpler words

Have no cares; but in everything with prayer and praise put your requests before God.

What was going on

Paul writes from prison to Philippi: rejoice, do not be anxious, the peace of God guards hearts; contentment in every state through Christ.

What it means

Don't let worry take over—pray and thank God, and tell Him what you need.

When the to-do list and the worry list are the same list.

Isaiah 40:31 (KJV)

KJV

But they that wait upon the LORD shall renew their strength; they shall mount up with wings as eagles; they shall run, and not be weary; and they shall walk, and not faint.

In simpler words

But those who are waiting for the Lord will have new strength; they will get wings like eagles: running, they will not be tired, and walking, they will have no weariness.

What was going on

In this passage of Scripture, the focus is this: Comfort and renewed strength — spoken by Isaiah (comfort from God) to Weary Judah — and anyone waiting on the Lord.

What it means

Those who wait on the Lord get new strength—they don't give out.

Sometimes the win is walking without fainting—not soaring.

Psalm 46:10 (KJV)

KJV

Be still, and know that I am God: I will be exalted among the heathen, I will be exalted in the earth.

What was going on

When the earth shakes and nations rage, this psalm declares God is a present refuge and strength — “be still, and know that I am God.”.

What it means

Be still and know that I am God; I will be exalted.

Stillness is a step, not a luxury you earn after finishing everything.

Galatians 6:9 (KJV)

KJV

And let us not be weary in well doing: for in due season we shall reap, if we faint not.

In simpler words

And let us not get tired of well-doing; for at the right time we will get in the grain, if we do not give way to weariness.

What was going on

Freedom in the Spirit; fruit of the Spirit; bearing one another’s burdens.

What it means

And let us not get tired of well-doing; for at the right time we will get in the grain, if we do not give way to weariness.

Weariness in good work is named honestly here.

2 Corinthians 12:9 (KJV)

KJV

And he said unto me, My grace is sufficient for thee: for my strength is made perfect in weakness.

In simpler words

And he said to me, My grace is enough for you, for my power is made complete in what is feeble. Most gladly, then, will I take pride in my feeble body, so that the power of Christ may be on me.

What was going on

In this passage of Scripture, the focus is this: Thorn and grace — spoken by Paul to Believers learning strength in weakness.

What it means

God's power shows up best when we're weak—His grace is enough.

When you cannot add one more thing, grace meets you in the cannot.

More on this topic

When it hits hardest

  • When everything is due at once—Matthew 11:28 before you re-sort the list for the fifth time.
  • Caregiving plus work plus home—Psalm 55:22 for the weight that has no neat category.
  • After a meltdown (yours or a child’s)—Psalm 46:10 for sixty seconds of stillness, then one small next thing.

A Gentle Word

Matthew 11:28. Come. Heavy laden. Rest. He will sustain you.
